extracted.intended_audience: writers and students seeking to study or emulate Jonathan Swift's satirical prose
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing prose in the manner of Jonathan Swift—satirical, rhetorically rigorous, and formally polished—covering sentence structure, diction, tone, and rhetorical techniques. Useful for creative writers, literary students, or anyone attempting to imitate Swiftian satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift employed a writing style characterized by sharp wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use biting, intelligent humor that critiques behavior or institutions; be pointed and incisive rather than merely whimsical. Wit should serve a satirical purpose, cutting to the underlying folly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift's style is characterized by clarity of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure arguments and observations are logically clear and easy to follow; avoid obscuring critique with gratuitous ornamentation. Clarity strengthens satire by making the target and the point unmistakable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust command of the English language
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift demonstrated a robust command of the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show mastery of vocabulary, grammar, and idiom to wield language precisely; confident, controlled prose lends authority to satirical claims and lets nuance come through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct yet intricate expression
rubrics_metrics.description: His style is often described as direct yet intricate, reflecting understanding of writing mechanics and human complexities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a surface directness (clear statements) combined with layered meaning (irony, implication). Avoid vagueness: be straightforward in presentation while embedding complexity beneath the surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical balance in sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift’s sentence structure typically showcases a classical balance, reminiscent of the prose of his time; he often used a formal, polished syntax that lent his arguments a compelling authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt well-constructed, balanced sentences with formal polish to create rhetorical weight and credibility. Use classical syntactic patterns when appropriate to evoke an authoritative voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of sentence types and lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: He was adept at employing a variety of sentences—complex and compound, short and punchy—to maintain rhythm and emphasize his points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate long, complex sentences with short, punchy ones to control pacing and emphasis. Use sentence variation deliberately to sustain reader engagement and highlight key ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise and evocative word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift favored a lexicon that was both precise and evocative; he had the knack for selecting the exact word to convey shades of meaning or to provoke thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words for exactness and connotation; prefer the single right word over many approximate synonyms. Precision enhances clarity and heightens satirical impact; evocative terms help provoke reader reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of irony through tonal contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Swift’s most notable techniques is his use of irony; he uses a calm and reasoned tone to deliver shockingly outrageous suggestions (example: 'A Modest Proposal'). The contrast between his reasonable tone and the absurdity of his proposals creates a powerful ironic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a calm, rational voice when proposing absurd or extreme positions so the contrast produces irony. Let the dissonance between tone and content force readers to question the target issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical devices: repetition and analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: He made effective use of rhetorical devices such as repetition and analogy to reinforce his arguments and ensure they resonated with his audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repetition to hammer home key points and employ analogies to make abstract critiques concrete. Deploy these devices to increase memorability and persuasive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eloquence and incisive language for satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift’s writing is marked by its eloquence, its incisive use of language, and its keen awareness of the power of satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance stylistic elegance with sharp critical edge: eloquent phrasing should serve the satirical objective rather than distract from it. Aim for language that is both beautiful and morally/critically piercing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive and memorable prose
rubrics_metrics.description: His skillful manipulation of rhetorical devices allowed him to craft prose that was not only persuasive but also memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose arguments and images that linger—use vivid examples, clear logic, and rhetorical structure so the piece convinces readers and remains striking after reading.
